extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: A final USPTO order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on a state-court disbarment, detailing grounds, procedures, notices, duties, and remedial restrictions for a registered patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a state court under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24; the OED Director may file a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline and issue a Notice and Order initiating the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order provides respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on the reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). The Notice and Order is to be published in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for exclusion: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discipline may be predicated on a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) — i.e., being disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State (e.g., disbarment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline here was predicated on the respondent's disbarment by the Supreme Court of the State of Nevada. The USPTO action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-court discipline findings and applicable professional conduct rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The state-court (Nevada) decision found violations of RPC 1.1 (competence); 1.3 (diligence); 1.4 (communication); 1.5 (fees); RPC 1.15 (safekeeping property); 1.16 (termination of representation); and RPC 8.4(b), (c) and (d) (misconduct).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific misconduct supporting those rule violations included: failing to diligently pursue client matters; knowingly obtaining money from clients under false pretenses; abandoning a law practice without properly terminating representation; failing to appropriately handle client files (abandoning files in a storage unit); falsifying a government document to deceive clients; and failing to cooperate with the bar investigation and proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy: exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: The appropriate discipline in this proceeding is exclusion from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusion commences on the date of the Final Order. The order directs specific follow-up actions (publication, notices, dissociation of customer numbers, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service requirements (publication and service by certified mail)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a Notice and Order (service demonstrated by certified mail receipts) and publish the Notice and Order in the Official Gazette for two consecutive weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision lists certified mail receipt numbers as proof of service and explicitly notes Official Gazette publication; publication supports that respondent had notice and an opportunity to respond under the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural consequence of failure to respond under § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response within the allotted time, the USPTO may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Analysis section states respondent's failure to file a response led to the determination that no genuine issue of material fact existed and that exclusion was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary notice and public availability of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director is to publish a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette and disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the OED FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order includes wording for the Official Gazette notice describing the respondent, registration number, basis for exclusion, and a URL for the FOIA Reading Room (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary enforcement agencies and courts pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where respondent is admitted, to courts where respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory post-discipline notification step under § 11.59 to ensure other authorities and the public are informed of USPTO disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to comply with the obligations set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 following discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order directs compliance but does not enumerate § 11.58 duties; practitioners should consult § 11.58 for specifics (e.g., notification of client matters, withdrawal procedures, and restrictions while excluded).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of respondent's name from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures the excluded practitioner can no longer electronically transact before the USPTO using previously associated credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on applying for or obtaining a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or be added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an affirmative bar on obtaining access to certain USPTO systems and accounts while excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (and related disciplinary regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing statutory/regulatory authority grounds the Office's power to impose reciprocal discipline and to require the follow-up measures ordered.
